name: Zan Gula
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal, Raimund Kastenholz, Ulrich Kleinewillinghöfer & Florian Lionnet. 2020. The Bua group noun class system: looking for a historical interpretation. Language in Africa 1(3): 181-215. [HAL halshs-03097143]
sources.note: Nothing. Zan Gula noun pairs from Sauer & Sauer's unpublished data are cited, some tone-marked (līllɛ́/līnnú, máálɛ́/mááy, sɔ̄wɛ̀/sōwì), most unmarked; no prosodic statement.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2020. Personal pronouns in Bua languages. Language in Africa 1(3). [HAL halshs-03097103, 45 pp.]
sources.note: Nothing on Zan Gula stress. §7 Zan Gula(1) draws on Ahmat & Weiss 2010 (unpublished 12-p. grammar sketch, Mongo): 'Data and comments concerning Zan Gula are extremely cursory.. Tones are usually not marked.' §8 Zan Gula(2) uses de Rendinger 1949 (pp. 184-190), 'of limited reliability'. The one mention of 'syllable stress' (§3.2) concerns Tun pronoun vowel variants, not Zan Gula.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal, Raimund Kastenholz, Ulrich Kleinewillinghöfer & Florian Lionnet. 2018. The Bua Group languages (Chad, Adamawa 13): A comparative perspective. In R. Kramer & R. Kießling (eds), Current approaches to Adamawa and Gur languages (Afrika und Übersee Beiheft 34), 53-126. Cologne: Rüdiger Köppe. [HAL author version halshs-03096908, 58 pp.]
sources.note: No stress statement for any Bua language. §4.4 Tones: Ɓa, Lua, Tun, Bolgo have three contrastive heights, Kulaal two. §5.5 Tones: Zan Gula data (Sauer & Sauer, unpublished) are 'relatively limited and not systematically marked for tones, so that we will in fact not comment on them here'; the Zan Gula row of Table 21 (noun tone correspondences) is mostly '?'. Names the Zan Gula sources: de Rendinger 1949, Faris & Meundeung 1993e (SIL survey), Sauer & Sauer unpublished wordlist; footnote 21 says the Sauer data suggest an ATR harmony system.
sources.venue: Current approaches to Adamawa and Gur languages (Afrika und Übersee Beiheft 34)

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 1988. Présentation sommaire du groupe Boua (Tchad) (Adamawa 13 de J.H. Greenberg). In D. Barreteau & H. Tourneux (eds), Le milieu et les hommes: Actes du 2ème colloque Méga-Tchad, 275-286. Paris: ORSTOM.
sources.note: Nothing on stress for any language. §2.1 Phonologie (pp. 281-282) covers only tun, lua, 'ba (three-register tone systems, word-level tone schemes) and kulaal (Pairault's two heights). Zan Gula ('goula de Zan', ~1,500 speakers at Zan and Chinguil) is only listed on p. 279; the only sources named for the Guéra Gula are colonial vocabularies (Joly 1935, de Rendinger 1949, Gabe 1950, Mouchet 1958).

sources.citation: de Rendinger, R. 1949. Contribution à l'étude des langues nègres du Centre-africain. Journal de la Société des Africanistes 19(2): 143-194 (Zan Gula material pp. 184-190).
sources.note: Oldest source with Zan Gula data; colonial vocabularies of this period sometimes carry an 'accent tonique' remark. Open on Persée but the PDF sits behind an altcha proof-of-work gate that scripted downloading does not pass.
sources.venue: Journal de la Société des Africanistes

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page zang1249 and Wikipedia 'Zan Gula language'
sources.note: Glottolog lists no descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) reference for zang1249, only overviews and subclassification comments (Pairault 1969: 12-13; Kastenholz 2017: 2; Boyeldieu et al. 2018). Wikipedia has no phonology and cites only Ethnologue.

sources.citation: Kastenholz, Raimund. 2017. La langue bolgo du Guéra (Tchad): Notes de recherche et matériel lexical. Working Papers of the Dept. of Anthropology and African Studies, JGU Mainz 172.

sources.note: Closest recent description of a Guéra Bua language (Bolgo) with explicit tone analysis; cited by Glottolog (p. 2) for Zan Gula subclassification. The Mainz URL given in the 2018 bibliography is dead (404).
sources.venue: Working Papers of the Dept. of Anthropology and African Studies, JGU Mainz 172

sources.citation: Ahmat, Oumar & Doris Weiss. 2010. Esquisse grammaticale du more [Zan Gula] (avec des annotations par Silke Sauer). Mongo: SIL Tchad, unpublished ms., 12 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only grammar sketch of Zan Gula that exists; a 12-page SIL sketch normally opens with a phonology/orthography note that would state tone and stress. Held by SIL Tchad (Mongo/N'Djaména) and by Boyeldieu/Kastenholz; not in any repository found.

sources.citation: Sauer, Silke & Martin Sauer. c. 2007-2011. Zan Gula (More) wordlist and orthography/phonology notes. SIL Tchad / APLG, Mongo. Unpublished (also any 'Précis d'orthographe' accompanying the 2007 and 2011 primers Alfi kîrra more!).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The Sauers designed the More orthography and supplied the tone-marked lexical data used in Boyeldieu et al. 2018/2020; their orthography guide or phonology statement is the most likely place for an explicit remark on tone vs. stress.
